profile.entities: Cyient DLM Ltd; Altek Electronics (US subsidiary, ITAR-certified); Mysore & Hyderabad units
profile.mgmt: Krishna Bodanapu (Non-Executive Chairman); Rajendra Velagapudi (MD & CEO); R.M. Subramanian "RMS" (CFO)
profile.subseg: Aerospace & Defence; Industrial; Medical (MedTech); Automotive/EV; (new lanes: Semiconductor cap-equipment, Robotics, AI/Data-Centre)

bull_bear.body: - Reinvesting into working capital (inventory as a "leading indicator" to protect deliveries through West Asia disruption) and into commercial-org build-out. No buyback/dividend signalled; disciplined, growth-stage EMS. IPO-proceeds utilisation continuing (from prior quarters).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Working capital / negative operating cash flow:** inventory build (DIO 162 days vs 153 QoQ) + lower customer advances (15 vs 18 days); NWC 161 days (vs 145). Mgmt expects cash flow to turn positive once growth-inventory normalises.
- **West Asia / geopolitics:** logistics delays and higher shipping cost; mitigated by strategic inventory and alternate sourcing — no Q1 impact, planning to shield Q2, but ongoing.
- **Forex:** large two-way (export + import) exposure → balance-sheet swings on rupee moves.
- **Customer concentration / lumpiness** in aerospace-defence; MedTech seasonally soft; new AI/data-centre lane is early and unproven with no disclosed products yet.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and execution-focused; Chairman Bodanapu credited CEO Velagapudi with the turnaround. Transparent on what they won't guide (absolute order-book, segment-wise new-lane %), consistent messaging on the SET roadmap. CFO candid ("aerospace is always an investment for the first few years"). No over-promising on AI/data-centre — repeatedly deferred specifics 2-3 quarters.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Book-to-bill held at 1.5x *for the full year* is effectively a soft growth signal — pair with "aspirational" growth rates and the record backlog to back into strong FY27 revenue.
- The AI/data-centre entry is deliberately capability-first, capex-light and unguided — optionality, not yet a numbers story; management flagged data-centre demand is inherently cyclical ("it's up now, it will go down") vs aerospace as the steady base.
- Industrial +90% YoY and Box-Build +85% YoY are the quarter's real engines, not aerospace alone — diversification is working.
- Margin ladder (9-11 → 11-13 → 13-18%) is explicitly product/lane-mix driven (B2S + new industries), giving a multi-year re-rating framework to verify against.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance-sheet priority is working-capital reduction: lower working-capital borrowings drove a 29% YoY fall in finance cost, and NWC days have been managed down from a 165-day peak into the ~145-161 day range.
- Customer advances have compressed from 33 days to 15 days over five quarters, meaning growth is increasingly self-funded rather than customer-funded.
- Operating free cash flow was negative INR 171 Mn for the quarter, reflecting reinvestment into inventory and B2S procurement ahead of the order book conversion.
- The deck makes no reference to dividends, buybacks or any equity/debt raise.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Industry mix:** Aerospace 42% (+40% YoY), Industrial 32% (+90% YoY), Defence 9% (+35% YoY), MedTech 16% (flat YoY — seasonal softness at one customer), Auto/others 1%.
- **Product mix:** PCBA 48% (+21% YoY), Box Build 41% (+85% YoY), Mechanical/others 10% (incl. B2S), Cables 1%.

- **Geography:** Rest-of-World 94%, India 6% (RoW led by aerospace/medical/defence/industrial customers outside India).

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Aerospace qualification moat (explicitly evidenced):** CFO — "The aerospace business is a double-edged sword. It's very, very difficult to get into. But once you are in you're in… that's a moat that's impossible to reach for a new entrant, and we're in the moat." Company is qualified with "every single major OEM or significant Tier-1 that buys any electronics" (Honeywell, Thales, Safran, BAE, etc.).
- **Certifications as barrier:** completed Nadcap audit (demanding aerospace-grade) for cable-harness at Mysore; ITAR-certified Altek unit — regulatory/qualification barriers that reinforce high-reliability positioning.
business.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position

business.body:
| Challenge (their words) | Beneficiary stock(s) — NSE · BSE · Sector | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| "China plus one shift is redistributing manufacturing globally… supply-chain resilience a strategic priority" + rising electronic content + AI-infra hardware demand | **CYIENTDLM · 543933** — High-Reliability EMS (self) ✅ | China-based / commodity high-volume EMS | Direct China+1 + electronics-content beneficiary; record book-to-bill 1.5x, RoW 94% revenue proves the outsourcing pull. **High** |
| "AI infrastructure will increase the need for sophisticated electronic manufacturing capabilities" — company entering AI/data-centre & robotics lanes | **CYIENTDLM · 543933** (self, prospective) ✅ | — | Emerging optionality only — sales team hired, no products/revenue disclosed yet. **Low-Med (unproven)** |

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Targets the high-reliability end of a ~$625-650B global EMS market seen reaching ~$1.1T by 2033 at ~6%+ blended CAGR, with the company arguing growth is faster in high-reliability than in commodity volume work.
- Core franchise sits in Aerospace & Defence, Industrial, Medical and Automotive, anchored on power electronics, where high-mix, low-volume, certification-heavy builds create switching costs.
- China+1 footprint realignment and supply-chain regionalisation are framed as the structural tailwind redistributing manufacturing toward Indian EMS players.
- Business is overwhelmingly export-facing: ROW accounts for 94% of the mix versus 6% India, the latter coming mainly from A&D, Auto and Medtech.
- Two new demand lanes are called out as adjacent extensions of the same stack: robotics (high-reliability subsystems, control electronics, test assemblies) and AI infrastructure / data centre hardware.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Order book] Order book of INR 2,598.9 Cr (INR 25,989 Mn) is the highest since IPO and has risen every quarter across the five-quarter series shown, from INR 21,318 Mn, giving multi-year revenue visibility.
- [Book-to-bill] Order intake of INR 551.9 Cr translated to a book-to-bill of 1.5x, sourced from both existing and new clients.
- [Semiconductor cycle] Chiplets, 2.5D/3D packaging and HBM are flagged as raising back-end equipment, test and assembly complexity, an adjacent opportunity for specialised EMS.
- [Leadership] Presented by Krishna Bodanapu (Chairman), Rajendra Velagapudi (MD & CEO) and Subramanian RM (CFO).
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- Normalized EBITDA margin 10.5% (+147 bps YoY from 9.0%); operating leverage + better revenue mix + disciplined cost the drivers ("filling the hopper").
- Sequential gross-margin dip from mix + pre-budgeted investment in commercial org; not structural.
- Finance costs −29% YoY on lower working-capital borrowings. Future margin step-up mapped to new higher-value lanes + B2S (+250-300 bps) rather than pure cost-out.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Revenue INR 3,738 mn (+34.3% YoY), EBITDA INR 392 mn (+56.2%, 10.5% margin, 4th straight double-digit qtr), PAT INR 163 mn (+118% YoY, 4.4%). Record order book INR 2,598 cr (+INR 1,832 mn QoQ), intake INR 551.9 cr, book-to-bill 1.5x. Aerospace 42% (+40%), Industrial 32% (+90%), Defence 9% (+35%), MedTech 16% (flat). Added 2 new logos (industrial+auto); B2S lab doubled to 15,000 sq ft; Nadcap audit cleared (Mysore); Rama Alapati joins as Chief Strategy & Growth Officer. SET roadmap articulated: margin ladder 9-11% → 11-13% (FY27-29, +Robotics/AI-DC) → 13-18% (FY30+, B2S/IP). Guidance: 1.5x book-to-bill for FY27; B2S +250-300 bps to consol EBITDA; no major capex. Working capital elevated (DIO 162d, NWC 161d), op cash flow negative.
- _next Q → check: revenue/margin momentum sustained; book-to-bill still ~1.5x; working-capital & op-cash-flow turning positive; B2S revenue starting; first AI/data-centre & robotics order intake + product disclosure; Honeywell/Thales ramp; MedTech recovery from seasonal dip._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Revenue growth:** No hard number given; "similar momentum" in revenue/order-intake range expected in Q2 and through FY27; CFO pointed analysts to "aspirational revenue growth rates" combined with the 1.5x book-to-bill (i.e. compute it).
- **Margin:** "Expand" phase (FY27-FY29) EBITDA margin **11-13%**; "Transform" phase (FY30+) **13-18%**. Core stack runs ~9-11% today. B2S adds **+250-300 bps** to consolidated EBITDA margin as it scales.
- **Order book / inflow target:** Book-to-bill **~1.5x maintained for the full year** FY27 (declined to give an absolute year-end order-book number).
- **Capex / commissioning:** No major expansion capex — only regular annual maintenance capex; existing installed capacity can support ~1.75-2x current revenue and new AI/robotics lanes need no additional capex.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- Record order book **INR 2,598 cr**; order intake **INR 551.9 cr** in the quarter (no lumpy one-off — broad-based across existing + new customers), book-to-bill **1.5x**.
- ~70% of intake from existing customers, ~30% from logos added in the last 4-6 quarters; management stresses "a lot of opportunity still" with existing accounts.
- Sales pipeline described as "substantially higher" than order book (well above the ~USD 0.5 bn / INR 4,000-5,000 cr an analyst floated) — not disclosed. Pipeline mix ≈ 48% aerospace & defence, <40% industrial/semiconductor cap-equipment, balance medical + small auto.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **SET roadmap:** Strengthen (today, 4 industries, ~9-11% margin) → Expand (FY27-29, add Robotics + AI/Data-Centre = 6 industries, 11-13%) → Transform (FY30+, own B2S products/IP, 13-18%).
- **B2S:** lab doubled 6,000 → 15,000 sq ft; strong order pipeline; meaningful revenue in the next 12-18 months; a Japan eVTOL/EAV customer (SkyDrive-type) in engineering-design stage, ~12-18 months to production, then whole-lifecycle build.
- **AI/Data-Centre & Robotics:** sales directors on board this quarter; order intake expected in FY27, revenue later; specific product lines (power supply/cooling/compute hardware) to be disclosed in 2-3 quarters; deliverable with existing capabilities.
- **Semiconductor cap-equipment:** building products for existing customers; revenue growth over next 6-12 months.
- **Honeywell Aerospace + Thales:** early builds of large multi-year wins now ramping — "extraordinary growth this year" and over the next 18 months.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality
